dedupe_keys.name: pynomad microscopic pedestrian simulation model tu delft

description: PyNOMAD is the Python version of NOMAD, a microscopic pedestrian simulation model. It models the movements of individual pedestrians in great detail, supporting studies of crowd dynamics in walking spaces. It was published by Martijn Sparnaaij, Mario Campanella, Winnie Daamen and Serge Hoogendoorn of the Department of Transport and Planning on 4TU.ResearchData in October 2023, with a reference to a TU Delft doctoral thesis. It is generic and can be applied to any walking infrastructure such as stations, terminals and public spaces. The source code is free under GPL-3.0 and can be cloned from the 4TU.ResearchData git repository or downloaded as a zip file. Caveats: the record gives only a short description, so users need the code and the thesis to learn the model's inputs and calibration, and it is a first published version. PyNOMAD supports agent-based simulation of pedestrian flows, capacity planning of stations and walkways, and evacuation studies. It complements the OpenSidewalks schema and the pedestrian network datasets catalogued here.
